question: In the context of local storms of hot weather season, Nor’Westers are:

options.text: the dreaded evening thunderstorms in Bengal and Assam
a nearby wind that blows coffee flowers in Kerala
the hot, dry and oppressing winds blowing in the Northern plains from Punjab to Bihar with higher intensity between Delhi and Patna
the pre-monsoon showers that are a common phenomenon in Kerala and coastal areas of Karnataka

solution:
The correct answer is __**the dreaded evening thunderstorms in Bengal and Assam**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nor'Westers** are the dreaded evening thunderstorms in Bengal and Assam.
 
• These storms are characterized by strong winds, heavy rain, and sometimes hail.
 
• They typically occur during the pre-monsoon season, providing relief from the intense heat of summer.
 
• Nor'Westers are locally known as **Kalbaisakhi** in West Bengal and Assam.
 
• These storms are crucial for agriculture in the region as they bring much-needed precipitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nor'Westers** are caused by the collision of dry, hot winds from the northwest with moist air from the Bay of Bengal.
 
• They are most frequent in the months of March to May.
 
• These storms can cause significant damage to property and crops but are also essential for the cultivation of rice and jute.
 
• Nor'Westers are part of the larger weather patterns affecting the Indian subcontinent during the hot weather season.
